scenes.text: But first... let's go to the gym. Heh. Don't worry, it's a short trip.
scenes.head: FIRST: THE GYM

scenes.text: In 2006, two economists studied 7,752 gym members.
scenes.head: 7,752 GYM MEMBERS
scenes.say: In two thousand six, two economists studied seven thousand, seven hundred fifty-two gym members.
scenes.show_source: Source: DellaVigna & Malmendier, "Paying Not to Go to the Gym", American Economic Review (2006)

scenes.text: The ones on monthly plans paid over $70 a month.
scenes.head: MONTHLY PLAN: $70+
scenes.say: The ones on monthly plans paid over seventy dollars a month.
scenes.show_source: Source: DellaVigna & Malmendier, "Paying Not to Go to the Gym", American Economic Review (2006)

scenes.text: Then they counted the visits. Guess how many per month?
scenes.head: HOW MANY VISITS?

scenes.text: ...Four point three.
scenes.head: 4.3 VISITS A MONTH

scenes.text: So every visit cost more than $17. A ten-visit pass? $10 a visit.
scenes.head: PER VISIT
scenes.say: So every visit cost more than seventeen dollars. A ten-visit pass? Ten dollars a visit.
scenes.show_source: Source: DellaVigna & Malmendier, "Paying Not to Go to the Gym", American Economic Review (2006)

scenes.text: They paid more... to go less. Ow.
scenes.head: PAY MORE. GO LESS.

scenes.text: The economists' explanation? People were overconfident about how often they'd go.
scenes.head: THE REAL REASON

scenes.text: Now flip it around. Why do companies love subscriptions so much?
scenes.head: WHY THEY LOVE IT

scenes.text: A subscription is money that shows up on its own. Every month. No new decision.
scenes.head: MONEY ON AUTOPILOT

scenes.text: My guess? Every new decision is a chance to say no. Autopay skips the decision.
scenes.head: NO DECISION. NO "NO".

scenes.text: And free trials? They're the welcome mat.
scenes.head: FREE TRIALS

scenes.text: In a 2026 Self Financial survey, about seven in ten people said they'd forgotten to cancel a free trial.
scenes.head: 7 IN 10 FORGOT
scenes.say: In a twenty twenty-six Self Financial survey, about seven in ten people said they'd forgotten to cancel a free trial.

scenes.text: Free for seven days. Then... not free. For a long, long time. Heh.
scenes.head: FREE... UNTIL IT ISN'T

scenes.text: Now, the exit door. The FTC has a name for tricks like this: dark patterns.
scenes.head: DARK PATTERNS
scenes.show_source: Source: FTC staff report "Bringing Dark Patterns to Light" (September 2022)

scenes.text: Designs that steer you into things you didn't plan. Like signing up in one click... and canceling through a maze.
scenes.head: 1 CLICK IN. A MAZE OUT.
scenes.show_source: Source: FTC staff report "Bringing Dark Patterns to Light" (September 2022)

scenes.text: The FTC's 2022 report lists the classics: ads disguised as content, key terms buried in fine print...
scenes.head: THE CLASSICS
scenes.say: The FTC's twenty twenty-two report lists the classics: ads disguised as content, key terms buried in fine print...
scenes.show_source: Source: FTC staff report "Bringing Dark Patterns to Light" (September 2022)

scenes.text: ...and subscriptions that are hard to cancel. Hmm. Sounds familiar.
scenes.head: SOUND FAMILIAR?

scenes.text: Which cancel button was the worst one YOU ever fought?
scenes.head: WORST ONE YOU FOUGHT?

scenes.text: Here's a real one. In 2023, the FTC sued Amazon over Prime sign-ups and cancellations.
scenes.head: THE PRIME CASE
scenes.say: Here's a real one. In twenty twenty-three, the FTC sued Amazon over Prime sign-ups and cancellations.
scenes.show_source: Source: FTC v. Amazon (filed 2023); settlement announced Sept 25, 2025 (AP, NBC News)

scenes.text: The FTC said Amazon's own nickname for that cancel process was... the Iliad.
scenes.head: ITS NICKNAME?

scenes.text: The Iliad! An ancient Greek poem about a ten-year war. Heh... for a cancel button.
scenes.head: AN EPIC... FOR A BUTTON

scenes.text: The complaint said that process took four pages, six clicks and fifteen options to get out.
scenes.head: 4 PAGES. 6 CLICKS. 15 OPTIONS.
scenes.show_source: Source: FTC v. Amazon (filed 2023); settlement announced Sept 25, 2025 (AP, NBC News)

scenes.text: In September 2025, Amazon agreed to pay $2.5 billion.
scenes.head: $2.5 BILLION
scenes.say: In September twenty twenty-five, Amazon agreed to pay two and a half billion dollars.
scenes.show_source: Source: FTC v. Amazon (filed 2023); settlement announced Sept 25, 2025 (AP, NBC News)

scenes.text: One billion in penalties, one and a half billion back to customers. Amazon admitted no wrongdoing.
scenes.head: WHERE IT GOES
scenes.say: One billion in penalties, one and a half billion back to customers. Amazon admitted no wrongdoing.
scenes.show_source: Source: FTC v. Amazon (filed 2023); settlement announced Sept 25, 2025 (AP, NBC News)

scenes.text: Reports said about 35 million customers could get refunds. Up to $51 each.
scenes.head: UP TO $51 EACH
scenes.say: Reports said about thirty-five million customers could get refunds. Up to fifty-one dollars each.
scenes.show_source: Source: FTC v. Amazon (filed 2023); settlement announced Sept 25, 2025 (AP, NBC News)

scenes.text: Fifty-one bucks. For a war poem. Heh... I'd read it for less.
scenes.head: FOR A WAR POEM
